ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every UBO, manager, general partner and authorized agent at formation and at each ownership change against: (1) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (2) EU autonomous sanctions lists as implemented by Luxembourg legislation; (3) OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists where cotton transactions touch USD or U.S. counterparties; (4) the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance national freezing decisions; and (5) CSSF public statements and enforcement lists. PEP screening must identify Politically Exposed Persons and close associates under Article 3(8) of Directive (EU) 2015/849, as transposed, and will trigger enhanced due diligence, documented source of wealth, and senior management approval prior to incorporation and account opening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCSL), https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The RCSL accepts names in French, German or English, but requires the corporate form suffix 'SCSp' or 'societe en commandite speciale'. Where the proposed name originates in a non-Latin script, a transliteration into Latin characters signed by a sworn translator is mandatory. The partnership agreement filed with the RCSL must be in French or be accompanied by a certified French translation. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCSL registered name or trademark and must not mislead as to the activity, legal form or public character of the entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name may be reserved via the LBR portal for an administrative fee and is held for 30 calendar days. If the RCSL rejects a name on grounds of identity, similarity or misleading character, the incorporator must file an administrative appeal with the Commercial Chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within 15 calendar days of written refusal, in accordance with Article 9 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the trade and companies register. The appeal must be lodged by a Luxembourg avocat a la Cour and attach the refusal letter, the proposed partnership agreement, a certified comparison of conflicting registry entries, and a written memorandum on distinctiveness. The tribunal typically issues a decision within eight weeks; alternatively, the applicant may submit an entirely new name without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or shared Luxembourg business address is accepted for SCSp formation, provided the RCSL-registered address is a real, serviceable address in Luxembourg and the partnership agreement designates a Luxembourg registered office. For international raw cotton brokerage, no statutory license is required, and initial substance can be met through the registered agent and mail-forwarding service. However, if the SCSp seeks to establish Luxembourg tax residence, maintain a bank account, or obtain an EORI/VAT number, the bank and Luxembourg tax administration may demand genuine economic substance, including management decisions being taken in Luxembourg or a Luxembourg-resident general partner. A purely letterbox structure with no management conduct will increase bank account refusal risk and may be challenged under Luxembourg general anti-abuse rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: unannounced on-site inspection by RCSL is rare for a non-licensed trading entity, estimated at below 10% per fiscal year. The probability increases to approximately 15-20% if the SCSp uses a virtual office and relies on a third-party corporate agent for accounting, given CSSF thematic AML inspections of corporate agents. Should a Luxembourg bank apply enhanced due diligence or an on-site visit before account opening, the likelihood of a physical or remote inspection of the registered office / substance is estimated at 25-40%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (reconstituted by the Law of 1 August 2013), notably Articles 1–10, 70–73 and 102–106; relevant provisions of the Law of 23 July 2016 relating to Reserved Alternative Investment Funds for SCSp use as a contractual fund vehicle
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Register of Commerce and Companies (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership agreement (contrat de société) and RCS registration filing submitted electronically through the Luxembourg Business Registers e-incorporation portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; no mandatory paid-in capital escrow account; partner contributions and tranches are freely defined in the SCSp partnership agreement
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription to partnership interests in the SCSp, as set out in the partnership agreement, is accepted and ratified by the general partner and the special partners. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the SCSp be established at [Registered Office Address], Luxembourg, and that this address be filed with the RCS. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the general partner [Name] is appointed Manager with exclusive authority to manage the portfolio, open bank accounts, negotiate and execute contracts for raw cotton bales, and supervise all ordinary and extraordinary operations. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed AML/KYC compliance officer and authorized filer with the RCS and tax authorities, and that any one of the authorized signatories may act alone.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of the SCSp partnership agreement and partner KYC documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (if notarization required) or external legal counsel; otherwise executed directly by the parties
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement in French or English, specifying the legal form, name, registered office municipality, purpose of cotton brokerage, contribution amounts, profit and loss sharing, and the powers of the general partner. Collect certified passport copies of all individual partners and, for corporate partners, articles of association, certificate of good standing, and ultimate beneficial owner information.
required_dossiers: Certified passports or ID cards of individual partners
Certificate of good standing and corporate constitutional documents for corporate partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the draft is incomplete or the RCS queries missing items, submit supplementary documents within 15 calendar days; if notarization is refused, revise the agreement to comply with Luxembourg mandatory partnership law and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS online single window (e-Justice / LBR portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed partnership agreement, RCS registration form, registered office consent letter, identification of the general partner, and proof of payment of the filing fee through the RCS electronic portal. After validation, obtain the RCS registration number and verify publication in the electronic compendium of companies (Recueil électronique des sociétés).
required_dossiers: Consent of the owner of the registered office premises
Power of attorney (if a representative files on behalf of the partners)
Receipt of payment of the RCS filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a request for completion (demande de complément), respond via the same portal with corrected or additional documents. In case of refusal, file an appeal with the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within two months of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT registration with the Luxembourg Indirect Tax Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) via MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Luxembourg VAT registration form (formulaire 1), indicating the business activity under NACE 46.20 (wholesale of agricultural raw materials) and providing the RCS certificate. The AEDT will issue a Luxembourg VAT number (TVA/LU) for the SCSp.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of the general partner/manager
Proof of the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is queried or held pending, respond to AEDT enquiries through MyGuichet.lu within the prescribed delay and provide certified French/German translations of any external documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial ownership declaration with the RCS (RCB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCB (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, file the RCB declaration through the LBR portal, identifying all beneficial owners (natural persons), their ownership percentage, and the nature of control exercised over the SCSp. Retain the confirmation receipt as proof of filing.
required_dossiers: Identifications and residential addresses of beneficial owners
SCSp partnership agreement (to evidence the control structure)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCB department requests clarification or supporting evidence, amend the declaration and file additional ownership-chain documentation with apostille or legalization as applicable; failure to cure may result in administrative fines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial licensing required for pure brokerage of raw cotton bales (ISIC 4620). If a physical office is leased, the local municipal administration (administration communale) handles ordinary building and occupancy permits, but no industrial manufacturing license is needed.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industry operating license required. The SCSp may carry out wholesale brokerage as an unregulated commercial activity in Luxembourg; an establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) is not required for wholesale trade under current Grand-Ducal regulations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – No EIA needed; the activity is purely commercial brokerage with no physical transformation, processing, warehousing, or manufacturing of cotton bales.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the brokerage activity itself. If the SCSp leases an office, it must comply with municipal waste collection requirements and, for any heating/air conditioning installations, the applicable 2021 energy performance regulations; no industrial wastewater or VOC thresholds apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for a pure brokerage company. However, any leased registered office must have a valid fire safety certificate (conformité incendie), comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 4 November 1994 concerning fire safety in buildings, and meet occupational safety and electrical installation standards; no industrial civil-defense clearance or structural load certification is necessary.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — Luxembourg Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Administration; single taxpayer portal: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.public.lu; commercial register: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Although the SCSp has no distinct legal personality and RCS registration is optional under the law of 23 July 2016 (mandatory only if it owns Luxembourg real estate), the operating SCSp is voluntarily registered with the RCS to obtain its identification number ('matricule'), open bank accounts and file VAT returns. Procedure: (1) execute the SCSp partnership agreement and appoint an authorised representative or corporate services provider; (2) file the registration application with the RCS via the e-justice portal (LBR) to obtain the matricule; (3) apply to the AEDT for VAT identification using the official Form 2, attaching the matricule, partner identity details and designation of the person responsible for VAT, whereupon the AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT number (LU + 8 digits); (4) the SCSp is fiscally transparent for direct tax purposes, so the ACD does not normally allocate a separate CIT taxpayer reference, and partners are identified through their own national tax numbers and the partnership allocation schedule; (5) if the SCSp has no Luxembourg establishment and is a foreign-owned operator, an approved Luxembourg fiscal VAT representative must be appointed to complete Form 2 and file VAT returns; (6) obtain an EORI number from the Customs and Excise Administration (Douanes et Accises) for export declarations of raw cotton bales.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) is a white-listed fiscally transparent partnership under Luxembourg income tax law (Article 175 L.I.R.); it is disregarded for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax, and partners are taxed directly on their distributive share. For VAT purposes, however, the SCSp is treated as a separate taxable person to the extent it carries out an independent economic activity (brokerage of ginned raw cotton), so it may invoice commission, charge VAT where applicable, and deduct input VAT; no entity-level income tax is levied on the SCSp itself.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' election; fiscal transparency of the SCSp is statutorily imposed. Available elections and mechanisms: (a) election/registration of the SCSp as a VAT taxable person with full input VAT deduction where it conducts an economic activity; (b) Luxembourg VAT grouping ('assujetti unique') may be available for financially, economically and organisationally connected taxable persons, subject to AEDT conditions; (c) for US federal tax purposes, the SCSp may file Form 8832 to elect partnership or corporate classification, creating potential hybrid mismatch exposure addressed by Luxembourg ATAD/hybrid mismatch rules (Law of 21 December 2018); (d) partners may elect joint annual tax filing arrangements and submit a binding partnership income allocation schedule ('répartition des revenus') to the ACD.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Luxembourg Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée), implementing EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic-nexus turnover threshold applies to Luxembourg-established traders: any person carrying out an economic activity in Luxembourg must register for VAT from the first taxable transaction. A statutory small-business exemption under Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Law applies only to taxable persons whose annual turnover does not exceed EUR 30,000 (exclusive of VAT), but this exemption is not available for the SCSp's export cotton brokerage, which will exceed the threshold and is therefore mandatorily subject to VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no mandatory B2B real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance API, or digital stamping regime currently in force. B2B invoices may be issued on paper or in electronic format (EDI/XML), provided the authenticity, integrity and readability requirements of Articles 226 et seq. of the EU VAT Directive are met. E-invoicing in PEPPOL BIS format is mandatory for invoices addressed to Luxembourg public-sector contracting authorities under the B2G e-invoicing framework. The EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (ViDA) proposal is expected to introduce digital reporting requirements and mandatory e-invoicing for cross-border B2B transactions by 2030, but no national law has yet transposed it.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to (a) the physical export of ginned raw cotton bales supplied by the SCSp or on its behalf to a destination outside the EU, evidenced by an accepted customs export declaration and proof that the goods left EU customs territory within the statutory deadlines; and (b) brokerage, commission and agency services rendered by the SCSp that are directly linked to the export of the raw cotton, supplied to a customer established outside the EU, or in respect of goods dispatched outside the EU, provided the services meet the place-of-supply rules and are effectively used and enjoyed outside the EU. The SCSp must obtain and retain the customer's foreign order, the commission agreement (ISIC 4620 brokerage contract), proof of dispatch, the validated SAD (MRN), and the inward remittance certificate evidencing receipt of the export proceeds in the Luxembourg bank account. Input VAT on purchasing, transport, warehousing and brokerage-related costs is recoverable to the extent the output supplies are zero-rated exports.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD) / Export Accompanying Document with MRN evidencing departure from EU customs territory
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing physical transport of the raw cotton bales to the non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT MT103) proving receipt of export proceeds on the Luxembourg bank account
Commercial invoice, brokerage/commission contract and LC or documentary collection instruments (SWIFT MT700/MT760)
Packing list, certificate of origin, weight/press receipts and third-country customs entry certificate (supporting evidence)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims on cotton brokerage are subject to AEDT audit under Article 69 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, with powers to inspect commercial books, customs records and bank statements. Where export evidence (SAD/MRN, transport documents or inward remittance certificates) is missing, false or fraudulent, the AEDT retroactively reassesses VAT at the standard 17% rate with default interest, denies input VAT deduction on related costs, and imposes clawback extending the full limitation period (generally 5 years; 10 years in cases of fraud). Administrative fines of up to EUR 25,000 per infringement may be imposed; criminal tax fraud sanctions include fines and imprisonment of up to five years under the Luxembourg Criminal Code and General Tax Law. The VAT fiscal representative (where appointed) and the jointly liable partners of the SCSp may be pursued in solidum for the reassessed VAT, interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank (ECB); prudential supervision of credit institutions, payment institutions and electronic money institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). The BCL is the sole authority for monetary policy implementation, foreign reserve administration and payment system oversight in Luxembourg, while the CSSF holds licensing, market-conduct, and AML/CFT supervisory powers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is the legal tender, having fully replaced the Luxembourg franc. As a Eurozone member and an IMF Article VIII jurisdiction, Luxembourg applies unrestricted convertibility on both current account and capital account transactions under TFEU Article 63 and Directive 88/361/EEC. There are no exchange controls, no conversion licensing gates, and no restrictions on profit remittance, partner distributions, liquidation proceeds, or cross-border payments. An SCSp is tax-transparent and not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax on distributions to non-resident partners; no CSSF or BCL consent is required for FX conversion or capital movements. The euro is a freely convertible reserve currency, with EUR/USD execution at market rates without administrative filters. The only residual obligations are statistical balance-of-payments reporting to the BCL and the EU Cash Controls Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 requiring a declaration for physical cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more across EU borders.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export proceeds under Luxembourg, ECB, or EU law. A Luxembourg commercial intermediary may retain export receipts freely in EUR or in foreign currency, including USD, in onshore or offshore accounts, and may convert at any time without central bank approval. For raw cotton bales moving through Luxembourg as a routing or brokerage platform, the operator must nonetheless comply with EU customs declaration requirements, Intrastat reporting, zero-rated export / reverse-charge VAT treatment, sanctions screening, and, if physical banknotes or bearer negotiable instruments cross the EU border, declaration at the EUR 10,000 threshold. There is no obligation to convert export proceeds into EUR and no time limit for bringing them back to Luxembourg.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: MEDIUM as an auxiliary settlement rail, LOW as a primary treasury bank. Luxembourg-licensed electronic money institutions and payment institutions, or foreign EMIs passporting into Luxembourg under Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2), may open payment accounts for the SCSp and provide multi-currency virtual IBAN collection, automated AP/AR workflows, rapid vendor payouts, and segregated escrow-style balances. Legal constraints: (i) the EMI must hold a valid CSSF authorisation or a passport notification duly filed with the CSSF; (ii) the EMI's risk appetite must expressly permit textile raw-materials commodity trade, as many global EMIs refuse cotton and soft-commodity flow; (iii) EMIs cannot issue, advise, confirm, or negotiate Letters of Credit, documentary collections, or bank guarantees because those instruments require a SWIFT-connected credit institution with trade finance capacity; and (iv) the tax-transparent unregulated SCSp structure triggers enhanced due diligence above relatively low transaction thresholds. Recommended architecture: hold the primary treasury, LC portfolio, and correspondent banking at a Tier 1 bank; use the EMI only as a segregated collections wallet or contractor-payment wallet for small-ticket disbursements with zero end-of-day balance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: As a default, Luxembourg Tier 1 banks require at least one natural-person authorised signatory, preferably the general partner's managing director or a fully empowered statutory agent, to attend an in-person KYC interview at the bank's premises in Luxembourg or at a recognised branch/notary abroad before the account of a non-resident SCSp is opened. The mandate derives from the risk-based approach set by the Luxembourg AML/CFT framework (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended by the Law of 17 July 2020, and CSSF Regulation 21/800): physical verification is not always statutorily mandatory, but face-to-face confirmation becomes a practical condition when UBOs reside outside the EU, the partnership is newly incorporated, or the commercial flow involves non-EU cotton suppliers. Remote opening is permitted only if the bank accepts certified video identification under eIDAS with qualified electronic signature, together with apostilled or notarised constitutional deeds, a certified RCS / LBR excerpt, and a legal opinion from a Luxembourg avocat confirming the signatory's authority. In general, at least the initial account-opening meeting remains physical for a non-resident SCSp.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, forced-labour, and country-risk exposure from raw cotton origin, particularly Xinjiang-origin bales subject to the US UFLPA prohibition, or West African cotton sourced from FATF grey-listed or high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., Burkina Faso, Mali), generating negative screening hits and enhanced due diligence under CSSF Regulation 21/800.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete supply-chain compliance bundle including: Chamber-of-Commerce Certificate of Origin; commercial invoice and packing list; full ocean Bill of Lading with vessel IMO number and cargo insurance certificate; UFLPA traceability dossier with grower-to-bale chain-of-custody declarations; forced-labour-free supplier attestations and codes of conduct; EU/AES customs export declarations or equivalent; SGS / Cotecna / Bureau Veritas / Intertek pre-shipment inspection reports; the sale contract with stated ICC Incoterms 2020; and a legal opinion confirming no US, EU, or UN sanctions nexus on parties, flag, vessel, or insurers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity of the SCSp, an unregulated partnership whose general partner is a professional service company and whose limited partners are non-resident investors, triggering the 'complex legal arrangement' red flag and multi-layer beneficial-ownership disclosure demands.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR / Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) excerpt; notarised or apostilled register of partners identifying every partner with a direct or indirect interest of 25% or more; an organisational chart linking all intermediate entities to ultimate natural persons; executed partnership agreement and deed of contribution; GP board resolutions with a delegation-of-authority matrix; senior-management CVs; and a professional AML opinion letter mapping the full control chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering and phantom-cargo red flags, including invoice mismatches, over/under-invoicing of cotton bales, round-tripping, abandoned shipments, or valuation gaps between contract price, inspection value, and the documentary collection or LC settlement amount.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Back-to-back trade dossier containing: signed purchase and sale contracts with clear Incoterms 2020 and price benchmarks (Cotlook A index, ICE Cotton No.2 futures) substantiating the invoice quantum; third-party pre-shipment inspection and weight certificates; packing lists; warehouse receipts issued by accredited storage operators; a consecutive bill-of-lading audit trail with live AIS/gateway vessel tracking; cargo insurance certificates; shortfall and hope letters; bank statements pairing each payment to the specific invoice and shipment; and the SCSp's statutory books evidencing commercial rationale and consistent gross margins.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance deficiency of the pass-through SCSp, featuring no employees, no independent decision-making, and a single administrative service-provider footprint, leading the bank to classify the entity as low-substance and to demand enhanced EDD or refuse onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg substance file containing: original or certified copy of the lease for the registered office or operating premises; detailed minutes of partner and GP meetings recording trade approvals, credit-risk analysis, and hedging decisions; appointment of an independent Luxembourg compliance officer or chartered accountant; a real-time operational trail with broker contracts, trade confirmations, and supplier correspondence; management accounts or financial statements evidencing active brokerage activity; and a corporate calendar demonstrating that the SCSp's sole economic purpose is international raw-cotton brokerage rather than passive capital parking.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from non-resident limited partners into the SCSp must be executed as SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers (or SEPA Credit Transfer for euro amounts) from the contributor's own account at a PSD2-licensed institution to the SCSp's IBAN at a Luxembourg Tier 1 bank, referencing a formal capital call notice. The remittance information field must state 'equity contribution to SCSp' together with the capital call serial number; for statistical purposes the transaction is classified as direct investment equity capital under the BPM6 framework, and, where the transaction reaches the Luxembourg balance-of-payments reporting threshold (EUR 12,500 per transaction), the remitter and the receiving bank must provide the required counterparty attributes. The bank requires at each draw-down: an executed capital call certificate, a deed of capital contribution, an updated register of partners, a source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statement, and evidence that the funds originate from a compliant banking system. No capital duty, stamp duty, or exchange-control permit applies to inbound contributions to an SCSp; the bank performs standard sanctions screening on the remitter and all intermediary banks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rails are: (1) SWIFT MT103 priority customer credit transfers for direct supplier advances, brokerage commissions, freight, and inspection fees, executed through the Tier 1 bank's correspondent network (EUR via TARGET2 and SEPA, USD via CHIPS/Fedwire, GBP via CHAPS); (2) irrevocable, confirmed Letters of Credit governed by UCP 600, and eUCP where electronic documents are tendered, issued in favour of cotton-origin suppliers, with the Luxembourg bank acting as confirming or advising bank, or the SCSp's bank receiving the L/C as beneficiary when the SCSp is exporter of record; (3) documentary collections under URC 522, either documents-against-payment at sight or documents-against-acceptance with tenor drafts, for recurring and lower-risk shipments; and (4) SEPA Credit Transfers for euro-denominated EEA service-provider and administrative payments. Each disbursement must carry purpose codes consistent with the customs invoice and underlying contract, be directed only to pre-approved counterparties, and reflect the Incoterms 2020 allocation of payment obligations. USD settlement for US, Brazilian, and West African cotton is standardised as sight or 30-day tenor LC, with negotiation against warehouse warrants only where held as cash collateral.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD deliverable foreign exchange forwards (plain vanilla, up to 12 months) via the Luxembourg bank's treasury desk under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or local FX master terms
FX swaps combining a spot purchase with a forward re-sale of USD to manage rolling liquidity without altering the underlying trade position
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) for hedging medium-term pre-export finance or working-capital structures linked to cotton purchase programmes
Vanilla EUR/USD purchased options, both calls and puts, for asymmetric protection on large-margin LC settlements

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic cotton-origin currencies without liquid deliverable offshore markets, such as XOF, XAF, BRL, or INR, which are permissible in Luxembourg since no prohibition exists, although EUR/USD remains the primary hedge

Commodity-price hedges through ICE Cotton No.2 futures or swaps, legally distinct from FX hedging but essential to protect gross margin, with clearing through EU CCPs and EMIR reporting obligations applied where the SCSp exceeds non-financial counterparty thresholds

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Registered Data (Déclaration Annuelle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month following the anniversary of initial registration in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register; filed electronically via the LBR e-space.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers administrative warning and a penalty of up to EUR 1,000 (approx. USD 1,080). Continued failure for two consecutive years exposes the SCSp to administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS and loss of legal standing for commercial enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Dépôt Annuel des Comptes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS (Recette du RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the financial year; for a calendar-year SCSp the default deadline is 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit accounts within the legal deadline entails monthly penalty increments, court-ordered filing at the expense of the partnership, and administrative fines up to EUR 1,500; repeated non-compliance is grounds for administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) – Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any direct or indirect ownership change, and as an annual recurring confirmation within one month after the anniversary of the initial RBE filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with UBO disclosure carries criminal sanctions including imprisonment of up to one year and/or a fine of up to EUR 125,000; continued default may also result in administrative enforcement actions and blocking of compliance certificates.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit by a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises is mandatory when the SCSp exceeds two of the three following thresholds: balance sheet total exceeding EUR 4.4 million, net turnover exceeding EUR 8.8 million, or average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Separate statutory audit requirements apply if the SCSp is a regulated fund vehicle under CSSF supervision (e.g., FIC, SIF, RAIF) or if the partnership agreement imposes an audit covenant.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (loi modifiée du 19 décembre 2002; chart of accounts plan comptable normalisé). IFRS as endorsed by the EU may be used for voluntary consolidated accounts or where required by the CSSF in a regulated fund context.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner or authorised manager shall file an annual RBE confirmation each year covering all direct and indirect beneficial owners with a holding of 25% or more. Any transfer of partnership interests must be reported within 30 days. The confirmation must be repeated annually even where no ownership change occurred, based on the anniversary of the initial declaration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (similar to Register of Members)
Register of General Partner and Managers (Directors registry)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – USD 18,000 (no mandatory audit for small below-threshold SCSp; voluntary or fund-level audit in the higher range).

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17.00% corporate income tax (CIT) on taxable income exceeding EUR 175,000 and 15.00% on the first EUR 175,000, plus 7.00% solidarity surcharge on the CIT and municipal business tax at a communal rate of 6.75% in Luxembourg City, producing an aggregate effective headline rate of approximately 24.94%. The SCSp is fiscally transparent and outside the charge to CIT at entity level; taxation occurs at the partner level only.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent: no entity-level Luxembourg CIT, net worth tax, or subscription tax on the partnership itself. A Luxembourg-resident corporate partner may claim a 100% participation exemption on dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings of at least 10% or an acquisition cost of at least EUR 1.2 million held for 12 months. The patent box grants an 80% exemption of net qualifying IP income for partners actively carrying on the cotton brokerage trade. The Notional Interest Deduction (NID) permits a deduction of 8% on new equity contributed to the qualifying commercial activity of the SCSp, subject to statutory caps.
